appraisal_events.evidence: Told merely that he was unkind, Bloch tries to apologize "selon le mode qui est justement celui de l'homme mal élevé, lequel est trop heureux... de trouver une occasion de les aggraver," piling on melodramatic protestations of tenderness and ending in a sob.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly names Bloch's apology as the characteristic move of a badly-brought-up man, framing his excessive, tearful protestations as self-aggravating theater rather than genuine remorse.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator directly labels Bloch's manner of apologizing as that of an ill-bred man, and his overwrought tears read as excessive rather than sincere, lowering him locally.
